conventions: The construct chain OSEH/OSE (HA)MELAKHAH is fused to the single English word 'workmen' under rule 30 at 34:10 (twice) and 34:17, headed on the participle, with the separately segmented article taking the written 'the' beside the fused unit and the chain's relational 'of' going to the fused rectum where the phrase is a genitive. Where the ASV instead writes a word for each morpheme, as 'all that did the work' at 34:13, the one-rendering condition is unmet and rule 2 splits it, the participle taking the supplied relative and the noun its own English.

In the double-accusative clause HESHIV ET-HAMMELEKH DAVAR, rendered 'brought back word to the king' at 34:16 and 34:28, the object marker takes the supplied 'to': the unmarked accusative holds the English direct-object slot and the English verb reaches the marked object through the preposition, which is rule 16's first family and the route rule 44's first limit sends such a word by. The same reading gives the marker the 'for' of 'to make beams for the houses' at 34:11. Do not leave such a preposition with the noun under rule 33 or mark the marker unrepresented.

The chapter writes three topicalizing or appositional expressions and only one of them answers to a morpheme: the 'even' of 34:24 is the marker's, because that marker stands on the appositive phrase the word introduces, while the 'even' of 34:33 and the 'As touching' of 34:26 are added, the clause's marker in the first standing on the divine name rather than on the infinitive phrase and no marker or preposition standing on the fronted nominal in the second. The count was run phrase by phrase, so a later reader finding two 'even's treated differently is seeing rule 16's limit applied, not a split.
report: Read all 33 verses end to end against the 73-lemma candidate table, plus the `added` units the table is blind to. No construction is analysed two ways without something in the source or the ASV licensing the difference; verdict no-change, patches empty.

The construct chain rendered 'workmen' is the closest thing to a split and is not one: fused as one unit at 34:10 (twice) and 34:17 under rule 30, with the separately segmented article taking its own written 'the' and the chain's 'of' on the fused rectum; split at 34:13, where the ASV writes 'that did the work' and each morpheme holds a rendering of its own, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet and rule 2 governs.

Preposition-plus-construct fusions are uniform across the chapter: LIPHNE/MILLIPHNE to 'before' (18, 24, 27 three times, 31), BEYAD to 'by' and 'to' (14, 16), MEAL to 'above' (4). The two splits, LEPHANAW to 'in his presence' (4) and MEAHARE to 'from following' (33), are exactly the cases where the ASV spends a separate word on each morpheme.

Object marker: aligned only where the ASV spends a word on the object relation - 'of' at 34:21 (inquire of), 'for' at 34:11, 'to' at 34:16 and 34:28 (the same double-accusative clause, treated identically both times), 'even' at 34:24. Every other occurrence is unrepresented. The chapter's two appositional 'even's diverge for the reason rule 16's limit gives: at 34:24 the marker stands on the phrase the word introduces, at 34:33 the clause's marker stands on the divine name, so that 'even' is added, as 'As touching' is at 34:26.

Copula placement at 34:12 (on the participle MUPHQADIM) and 34:13 (on the predicate AL) is one principle read off the Hebrew predicate under rules 20 and 49, not two treatments of AL. Articles in demonstrative phrases are unrepresented in all six occurrences (21, 24, 25, 27, 28, 31), and the six supplied English objects with no object morpheme in the clause (4 twice, 10, 11, 12, 27, 32) are added throughout, none folded into a neighbouring verb.

BSB: all 30 disagreements are the documented convention differences - To under rule 16, R under rules 27, 40 and 52, Td under rules 41 and 47. The single item outside a recurring class, 34:3 the enclitic suffix on OD, is a choice between two co-referring morphemes for one English 'he'; giving it to the written independent pronoun is defensible and BSB's is a convention difference, not an error. No accepted edge was changed.

No promotion: the three things this chapter exercised hardest - a construct chain fused to one English noun beside its own article, a marker taking a supplied preposition, and a belonging LE rendered 'pertained to' - are already written into rules 30, 16 and 49 with examples of the same shape, so any rule here would restate them.
